correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the classical inclusion–exclusion count is E_n=3^n−(n+1)2^n+n(n+1)/2. On n=2t+ε, differences of the surviving triangular term are (t−s)[2(t+s+ε)+1], while differences of the exponential term have 2-adic valuation 3+ν₂(t−s). Thus the surviving expression is an isometry separately on each parity parameter t and permutes every quotient modulo 2^k. A block of 2^(k+1) consecutive indices contributes a complete quotient on each branch. The correction vanishes from N_k=max(3,2⌈k/2⌉−1): for odd k use n≥k; for even k the only possible exception in the range is n=k−1, with even n+1. For k≥5 the preceding index is even and below k, so its correction does not vanish; its translate by the period equals the uncorrected residue and is different. Sliding the preceding block to the first good block replaces just those two unequal residues, proving sharpness even for the unrefined histogram. The increment 2^k has valuation k−1 in the output differences on the tail, so the least tail period, which divides 2^(k+1), cannot be any smaller divisor. For k≤4 the natural domain boundary is sharp. An independent bounded modular check on k=1,…,10 corroborated parity fibers in the onset block, agreement with the reduced expression across two periods, and the preceding-index obstruction. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; its finite coverage is not the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives exact residue frequencies on any sufficiently late moving window for a natural Eulerian column, determines the parity of both preimages, and gives the shortest possible period and earliest uniform-window threshold. The parity isometry structurally explains the distribution; the exact moving-window threshold detects the initial correction and is stronger than asymptotic equidistribution or calculating a few moduli.
